title: What's New in Kotlin Jump
tagline: Memory that came back after shutdown
summary: Releasing a cache achieves nothing if the scan already running hands its megabytes straight back. That is what happened to all three of the features that hold the project listing, a second or two after the extension shut down.

highlights.title: Shutdown is now a stop sign
highlights.description: Each of the three refuses to write its listing once shut down: 40.8 MB for the quick fixes, 40.8 MB for the resource badge, about 17 MB for the reverse string map.

highlights.title: The window you actually hit
highlights.description: The scan takes seconds, one round trip per file, so closing the window while it runs is the ordinary case rather than a corner case.

sections.heading: Fixes
bullets: A scan in flight could repopulate the cache of a provider that had already been disposed, so the memory outlived the extension.
The same guard already covered the settings being switched off; shutdown was covered nowhere.
